title: Class scores
summary: Keep a class list with scores, add and drop students by command, then print the top three and the average.
prompt:
Write a class score keeper. Keep two lists side by side: one with names, one with scores, so position 0 in both is the same student.

Ask Command? again and again. Every command is one of:
- add NAME SCORE: add the student and their whole-number score at the end of both lists
- drop NAME: take that student out of both lists. If there is no such name, print No student called NAME.
- done: stop asking

At the end, if nobody is left, print No students. Otherwise print the names in the order they were added, joined with a comma and a space. Then print Top three: and up to three lines with the place, name and score, best first (on a tie, the one added first goes first). Last, print the average score with 1 decimal. Do not change the two lists while finding the top three: work on copies.

The example adds Ana, Ben, Cy and Dee, then drops Ben.
output:
Command? add Ana 82
Command? add Ben 67
Command? add Cy 91
Command? add Dee 74
Command? drop Ben
Command? done
Students: Ana, Cy, Dee
Top three:
1. Cy 91
2. Ana 82
3. Dee 74
Average: 82.3

steps.text: Make two empty lists, names and scores. Write a while True loop that asks Command? and splits the answer into a list of words called parts. If the first word is done, break.
For add, append the name to names and the score, as a whole number, to scores.
For drop, check the name is in names. If it is, find its position with index and pop that position from both lists. If not, print the No student called message.
steps.hint: i = names.index(parts[1]), then names.pop(i) and scores.pop(i).

steps.text: After the loop, if names is empty print No students. Otherwise print Students: and the names joined with a comma and a space.

For the top three, copy both lists. Up to three times: find the biggest score left with max, its position with index, print the place, name and score, then pop that position from both copies. Stop early if the copies run out.
steps.hint: left_scores = scores[:] makes a copy. for place in range(1, 4): and break when len(left_scores) == 0.

steps.text: Print the average: the sum of the scores divided by how many there are, with 1 decimal.

Command? done

tests.stdout:

Command? drop Zed
No student called Zed.
Command? add Ivy 60
Command? done

Top three:
1. Max 60
2. Ivy 60

Command? drop Bo
Command? done
